Loving Without Expectation of Return.
You know, it’s natural to hope that people notice our kindness. We want to feel appreciated—who doesn’t? We hope that the love we give will come back to us. But the deepest kind of love? That’s the love you give freely, just because you care, with no strings attached.
Most of us, even if we don’t admit it, keep a little scorecard in the back of our minds. We remember what we’ve done for others, and sometimes, we quietly wonder if it’s coming back our way.
Let me share a story with you. There was a woman who spent years caring for her aging father. She cooked for him, kept track of his medications, and sat by his side through long, quiet evenings. Some days, he’d thank her. Other days, he’d be distant or even a little grumpy. She sometimes wondered—does any of this matter? Is he even noticing?
But she kept showing up. Not because she was waiting for a thank you, but because she loved him. After he passed away, she discovered something unexpected—a stack of letters he’d written but never sent. Each one was filled with gratitude and love. In that moment, she realized just how deeply her love had mattered, even if she couldn’t see it at the time.
Most of us don’t realize how much we crave recognition. It stings a little when our kindness goes unnoticed or when relationships feel one-sided. But here’s something to remember: love, at its heart, is a gift. We don’t give it to get something. We give it because all of us need a little grace.
I remember a neighbor who told me how he mowed the lawn for an elderly couple every single week. They rarely said thank you. Sometimes, they’d even complain about the way it was done. But he kept showing up, week after week. Years later, after the couple had moved away, he got a letter from their daughter. She thanked him for his faithfulness and shared how much it had meant to her parents—even if they never found the words to say so.
Loving without expectation? It’s not easy. It means you risk feeling disappointed. It means letting go of your need for approval and trusting that love is enough on its own.
But here’s the thing—over time, loving like this changes you. It makes your heart more generous, more resilient, and, honestly, a lot more free.
